name: Operational patience
description: The adversary enforces deliberate pacing of all operational activities to prevent OPSEC failure caused by impatience or time pressure. Rushing causes: skipping verification steps; clipboard paste errors revealing sensitive data; sending messages to wrong recipients; bypassing anonymisation steps. Operational patience treats every step as requiring conscious verification before proceeding, regardless of counterparty time pressure.

subtechniques.name: Verify clipboard contents before sending
subtechniques.description: Before sending any message, the adversary explicitly verifies clipboard contents to ensure the correct text is being transmitted. Clipboard paste errors are a documented failure mode — pasting the wrong item can inadvertently transmit sensitive plaintext or unencrypted content intended for a different context.

subtechniques.name: Resist counterparty time pressure
subtechniques.description: When a counterparty attempts to rush an operation, the adversary deliberately slows down rather than complying. Urgency from counterparties is a known vector for inducing OPSEC failures and may indicate a test or undercover operation.
